supporting_observations.claim: The alerted HTTPS activity is to update.ledgerlink.com and is associated with C:\Program Files\LedgerLink\ledgerlinkupd.exe (PID 4152). The process launched at 13:39:11, and network telemetry associates it with the connection at 13:39:27.

Further connections to the same LedgerLink update host occurred at 13:43:51, 13:48:52, 13:53:58, 13:59:14, 14:04:11, and 14:09:13; endpoint network events identify the same updater process for these connections.

The observed connection timing is approximately five-minute recurrence, consistent with the inventory’s stated LedgerLink updater check interval. One attempt, at 13:53:58, received a proxy gateway error (503); later checks succeeded in establishing tunnels.
The updater process exited at 14:09:35, shortly after the final observed check.

known_telemetry_limitations: DC-SUN-01 winsec collection was unavailable from 13:30 to 14:00 UTC due to a log collection outage; this limits domain-controller event visibility during part of the review window.
The provided records show LedgerLink updater checks beginning at 13:39:27, but do not show corresponding checks earlier in the alert’s stated 13:30–14:10 interval.
The LedgerLink proxy records show CONNECT tunnel metadata rather than inspected HTTPS application content, so they do not reveal the full request or response payload.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish the contents of the encrypted LedgerLink HTTPS exchanges or whether an update was downloaded.
The evidence does not independently validate the LedgerLink executable’s integrity or the reputation of the remote service.
unrelated_findings: Unapproved cloud-service activity for separate review: a Dropbox Update connection to desktop.dropbox.com is recorded at 13:46:27 (T256-00316), and Firefox accesses a Google Sheets document at 14:05:09 (T256-00457). The inventory states that services other than approved services such as Microsoft 365/OneDrive are not approved; these events are not shown to be part of the LedgerLink alert.

Potentially unusual workstation activity for separate review: max.fischer ran PowerShell with ExecutionPolicy Bypass on C:\Admin\update-inventory.ps1 (T256-00155, T256-00156), followed by command-line and WMI system/service discovery activity (T256-00162, T256-00172, T256-00174, T256-00271, T256-00276, T256-00278). The records do not link these actions to the alerted HTTPS connections.
